zh_summary: @jsblokland: Mario Draghi, remembered for "whatever it takes," now says the bar is high for the ECB to step in to contain widening French bond spreads.
en_summary: @jsblokland: Mario Draghi, remembered for "whatever it takes," now says the bar is high for the ECB to step in to contain widening French bond spreads.
text:
The bar is high!

Former ECB President Mario Draghi will forever be remembered for three magical words: “Whatever it takes.”

At the height of the European debt crisis, those words helped save the euro.

Now, Draghi says the bar is high for the ECB to step in and contain the widening spread on French government bonds.

“There is nothing that says that these instruments cannot be used when a country is under Excessive Deficit Procedure. But certainly the bar is a little higher for that use.”

Meanwhile, France stands out in the IMF's latest World Economic Outlook as the only advanced economy facing a downward revision to its growth forecast.

Growth is expected to be a measly 0.4% this year, with a budget deficit exceeding 5% of GDP.

And elections approaching.

With that combination, I expect bond markets to keep testing the ECB's willingness to intervene by pushing French spreads even wider.

France has become the euro zone's weakest link.

Goodbye!
